rapport.title: Build rapport fast (Talk playbook)
rapport.try: Eyebrow-flash and warmly greet everyone you meet today, then count who flashes back.

calm.title: Calm someone down (Talk playbook)
calm.try: Next time someone is upset, say one true thing they can't disagree with, then pause.

support.title: Support someone who's struggling (Talk playbook)
support.try: Next time someone's replies get shorter, stop talking and count to nine in your head.

argue.title: When an argument gets heated (Talk playbook)
argue.try: In your next disagreement, ask what a heavy word means to them before you answer it.

H11.move: Reflect what their day probably felt like ("You must be shattered") purely to show you understand them.

H13.move: Share something real of your own first, at the depth you'd be happy for them to match, so it's easier for them to open up.

H14.move: When you genuinely don't know, show real interest in their expertise and let them teach you.

V68.move: Notice brief flashes of the seven universal expressions and respond kindly to the feeling you see.
V68.watch: A face only tells you a feeling. Respond to it; never treat it as proof of anything.

H41.watch: A change usually means stress or discomfort. Ask gently; never jump to a conclusion.

H15.watch: Never say "you're a significance person". The needs are hunches to test by listening, never labels.

H18.watch: Speak in their terms to be understood, never to steer a pitch.

H17.watch: Only ever give the honest reason. If it isn't true, don't say it.

n-ch-about.mv: A former US Navy behaviour trainer who teaches body language, composure and people skills through The Behavior Ops Manual (2023) and NCI University.
n-ch-about.tr: Tap the Chase Hughes filter above to study his cards on their own.

versions.title: Conversation starters
versions.note: Same aim in both books: skip autopilot small talk. Captivate gave you novel 'sparkers' and taught you to watch for what lights people up; Conversation turns that into nine power questions across three levels.

steps.label: Updated
steps.text: Nine power questions in three levels — put people at ease, connect deeply, create meaning.

versions.title: Finding common ground
versions.note: Hunting for three things in common became one quick phrase you say out loud the moment it's true.

versions.title: Introducing people

versions.title: First impressions
versions.note: From three body basics, to a full kit of charisma cues, to choosing your very first words.

versions.title: Reading faces
versions.note: From spotting seven expressions in others, to also checking the signals you send. Both say: respond to the feeling.

versions.title: Mirroring

versions.title: Stories

versions.title: Asking for advice
versions.note: Asking for advice moved from a liking trick into high-stakes talks, alongside appreciation, safety and a shared mission.

versions.title: Showing you like people

versions.title: Expecting the best

versions.title: Reading personality

versions.title: Self-stories
versions.note: From three story types in 2024, to five in the book, to the idea that stories can be rewritten.

steps.label: Earlier
steps.text: She described three self-stories from new research: someone who overcomes, someone who gives to everyone, and someone who feels nothing they do changes things.

steps.label: Latest
steps.text: She adds that self-stories are editable and tend to come true: people who see themselves as lucky spot more chances. Helping someone rewrite their story is the deepest goal of conversation.
